topics.name: Quadratic formula and nature of roots

questions.title: (1 − p) is a root: find the roots
questions.text: If (1 − p) is a root of the quadratic equation x² + px + 1 − p = 0, then its roots are:
steps: ① A root satisfies the equation: put x = 1 − p
③ Take (1 − p) common: (1 − p)[(1 − p) + p + 1] = 0
⑤ Equation becomes x² + x = 0 ⟹ x(x + 1) = 0
questions.remember: 'k is a root' ⟹ put x = k in the equation. It must give 0.
questions.trap: Expanding everything. Taking (1 − p) common is much faster.
questions.tryit: If x = 2 is a root of x² + kx − 6 = 0, find k.

questions.title: Equal AND positive roots
questions.text: The value of 'a' for which ax² + x + a = 0 has equal and positive roots is:
steps: ④ Positive root ⟹ −1/(2a) > 0 ⟹ a must be negative
questions.remember:
D > 0: two distinct real roots
D = 0: two equal real roots
D < 0: no real roots
questions.trap: Stopping at a = ±1/2 and picking 1/2. 'Positive roots' needs a < 0.
questions.tryit: Find k so that x² − kx + 9 = 0 has equal roots.

questions.title: √3x² − kx + 2√3: real equal roots
questions.text: If the roots of the quadratic equation √3x² − kx + 2√3 = 0 are real and equal, the value(s) of k is/are:
steps: ② Real and equal ⟹ D = b² − 4ac = 0
questions.trap: Writing √3 × 2√3 = 2√9 and stopping there. It's simply 6.
questions.tryit: For what k does 2x² + kx + 3 = 0 have equal roots?

questions.title: Assertion–Reason: conjugate surd roots
questions.text:
Assertion (A): If 5 + √7 is a root of a quadratic equation with rational co-efficients, then its other root is 5 − √7.
Reason (R): Surd roots of a quadratic equation with rational co-efficients occur in conjugate pairs.
opts: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
steps: ② Rational a, b, c ⟹ the surd can come only from ±√D
③ So surd roots come as p + √q and p − √q  ✓ R true
④ 5 + √7 is a root ⟹ the other is 5 − √7  ✓ A true
⑤ A follows directly from R
questions.remember: The ± in (−b ± √D)/2a is why surd roots come in pairs.
questions.trap: Forgetting 'rational coefficients'. Without it, the rule doesn't hold.
questions.tryit: Form the quadratic with roots 5 + √7 and 5 − √7.

questions.title: Discriminant of 4x² − 5 = 0
questions.text: Find the discriminant of the quadratic equation 4x² − 5 = 0 and hence comment on the nature of roots of the equation.
steps: ⑤ D > 0 ⟹ two distinct real roots
questions.remember:
D > 0: two distinct real roots
D = 0: two equal real roots
D < 0: no real roots
questions.trap: Taking b = −5 because it's the second number written. Here b = 0 and c = −5.
questions.tryit: Find the nature of roots of 2x² − 3x + 5 = 0.

questions.title: Solve x² + 2√2x − 6 = 0
questions.text: Solve the quadratic equation: x² + 2√2x − 6 = 0 for x.
steps: ① Need two numbers: product −6, sum 2√2 ⟹ 3√2 and −√2
questions.remember: Split the middle term: two numbers with product = ac and sum = b. Surds are allowed!
questions.trap: Thinking surds can't be split. 3√2 × (−√2) = −6 works perfectly.

questions.title: p for equal roots of px(x − 2) + 6 = 0
questions.text: Find the value of 'p' for which the quadratic equation px(x − 2) + 6 = 0 has two equal real roots.
steps: ⑤ p = 0 or p = 6;  p = 0 gives 6 = 0 (not quadratic) ✗
questions.remember: Always write the equation in standard form ax² + bx + c = 0 before finding D.
questions.trap: Keeping p = 0. Then there's no x² term, so it isn't quadratic. Reject it!
questions.tryit: Find k so that kx(x − 3) + 9 = 0 has equal roots.

questions.title: Consecutive negative integers: squares sum 481
questions.text: Find two consecutive negative integers, sum of whose squares is 481.
steps: ① Let the integers be x and x + 1
questions.remember: Consecutive integers: x and x + 1. Consecutive odd/even: x and x + 2.
questions.trap: Giving 15 and 16. The question says NEGATIVE integers.
questions.tryit: Two consecutive positive integers have product 306. Find them.

questions.title: The park and the pool (5 marks)
questions.text: In a rectangular park measuring 50 m × 40 m, the gram panchayat plans to construct a rectangular swimming pool in the middle, surrounded by a uniform width grass strip throughout the park. Find the dimensions of the swimming pool, if the area of the grassy strip is 1184 m².
steps: ① Strip width x on BOTH sides ⟹ pool (50 − 2x) × (40 − 2x)
⑥ x = 37 is too big (50 − 74 < 0) ⟹ x = 8
questions.remember: A uniform strip of width x reduces EACH dimension by 2x.
questions.trap: Writing 50 − x. The strip is on both sides!
questions.tryit: A 20 m × 15 m garden has a path of width x inside; the inner area is 126 m². Find x.

questions.title: Case study: 200 tiles or 128 tiles
questions.text:
A rectangular floor can be completely tiled with 200 square tiles. If the side of each tile is increased by 1 unit, it takes only 128 tiles to cover the floor.
(i) Taking the side as x units, form a quadratic equation.  (ii) Write it in standard form.  (iii) Find x by factorisation [OR by the quadratic formula].
steps: ⑥ x = 4 or −4/9;  a side can't be negative
questions.remember: Same floor ⟹ (number of tiles) × (area of one tile) is equal both times.
questions.trap: Writing 200x = 128(x + 1). Tile AREA is x², not x.
